insights.title: Where I'm covering, you're entering
insights.body: Josh waits for confirmation at support before shorting, but support is where the short is already over. The entry is at resistance; support is the exit.
insights.said: where I'm covering, you're trying to enter

insights.title: Right action, wrong side
insights.body: Taking action at a key point was correct; the direction was backward. The zone Josh shorted was a buy zone for calls.
insights.said: It was the right action, but the wrong side

insights.title: Fundamentals beat chart bias after earnings
insights.body: A massive earnings beat is a reason to look for a way to buy, not short. The crowd on X shorting it was a contrarian tell.
insights.said: why would you play a stock that just had earnings without looking

insights.title: Rates are repricing everything
insights.body: Rates up ~10x since 2021 and 125 bp in six months is forcing a repricing. The Mag 7 look toppy, so the edge is in rejections, not bounces — until rates get relief.
insights.said: You can't have rates this high and not

insights.title: Options give you two ways to be wrong
insights.body: A ~48-hour contract after earnings has to be right on direction and timing at once, and theta bills you while you wait.
insights.said: you need to be right on the time and the price

insights.title: Levels aren't arbitrary
insights.body: The numbers he gives line up across the screen and across timeframes — that's why 1,028–1,033 held on MU a week later.
insights.said: it's not like I throw arbitrary numbers out

insights.title: Pick the points that matter
insights.body: Being a perfect chartist isn't the goal. Find the few points that change the decision (double top, big gap, all-clear) and talk yourself through the action.
insights.said: I don't want you to get so much lost in trying to be a perfect chartist

insights.title: Learn to fish: scan the names that move
insights.body: When an unfamiliar name pumps (IBM), ask why and check where it's pumping into. That's how you find the next play yourself.
insights.said: you're learning to fish, you gotta learn to fish

insights.title: A lotto loss is small; 40% is reckless
insights.body: Jason's own failed lotto cost about $100. Putting 40% of an account into one short-dated trade is a different category of risk.
insights.said: taking, you know, 40% of your account size into a trade is crazy

insights.title: October: rough early, strong late
insights.body: Seasonally October starts weak and finishes strong into the year-end rally — and this year the midterms may flip control without changing the rate policy that's driving prices.
insights.said: October, which is typically a rough month in the beginning
